business_problem: Airbus wanted to reduce the manual effort and inconsistency involved in tracking major assembly steps and inspecting aircraft builds, where technicians had to watch, remember, and log work by hand.
solution_summary: Accenture Labs and the Airbus China Innovation Centre built a computer-vision inspection workflow that analyzes aircraft-assembly video feeds to detect completed tasks and manufacturing issues automatically. The program started as a proof of concept focused on final aircraft assembly, where manual logging and human judgment slowed the inspection process. Airbus specialists supplied manufacturing-domain knowledge and data requirements, while Accenture researchers created both a custom data annotation tool and a deep-learning AI model tuned for Airbus video. Treating the source material as video rather than disconnected frames allowed the team to annotate more data at scale and train the model faster. In production use, the system reads live or recorded video feeds, recognizes assembly milestones such as wing attachment, timestamps the events, and flags issues for follow-up. The result is a more automated quality-inspection flow that improves consistency, reduces manual effort, and frees technicians to focus on higher-value work.
